'''Tyler Paul Zeller''' (born January 17, 1990)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tyler Zeller Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/z/zellety01.html|access-date=2020-11-07|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en}}</ref> is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]]. As a freshman, he played on their [[2008–09 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|2009 national championship team]] and as a senior was an [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] and the [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Atlantic Coast Conference Player of the Year]]. He is the nephew of former NBA player [[Al Eberhard]], and the brother of fellow NBA players [[Cody Zeller]] and [[Luke Zeller]].

==Early life==
Born in [[Visalia, California]],<ref name="UNC Bio">{{cite web |url=http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/zeller_tyler00.html |title=Tyler Zeller |publisher=University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill Athletic Department |access-date=March 12, 2011 |archive-date=March 13, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110313081902/http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/zeller_tyler00.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Tyler Zeller grew up in [[Washington, Indiana]], attending [[Washington High School (Washington, Indiana)|Washington High School]]. In his four years at Washington High, his team won four sectional titles, as well as state Class 3A championships in his freshman and senior years (2005 and 2008). In his senior year, he averaged 33.1 [[point (basketball)|points]] and 11.0 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game, and also shot 69% from the field and 82% from the [[free throw]] line. In his final high school game, the '08 Class 3A final against [[East Allen County Schools|Fort Wayne Harding]], he scored 47 points, which broke a record for scoring by a player in an Indiana boys' state championship game that had stood since 1970. He was not only a basketball superstar, but also played on Washington High's [[tennis]] team for three years, and finished his high school career with a 3.99 [[grade point average]] on a 4.0 scale, good for third in his graduating class. After the 2008 season, he was named [[Indiana Mr. Basketball award|"Mr. Basketball"]] in Indiana, the state's highest honor for high school players. He received the title three years after his brother Luke and three years before his brother Cody were honored with the same award.  He was also named a [[McDonald's All-American Team|McDonald's All-American]],<ref name="UNC Bio"/> as well as a first-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]].

During the early stages of the signing period in November 2007, Zeller signed a [[National Letter of Intent|letter of intent]] to play at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]]. When the university announced his signing, [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|Tar Heels]] head coach [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams]] said about Zeller, "I think he is the finest running big man in the country and he has a tremendous shooting touch to go with that ability to run the floor."<ref name=Signing>{{cite press release |url=http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111407aad.html |title=Tar Heels Sign Three To NCAA Letters Of Intent |publisher=University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill Athletic Department |date=2007-11-14 |access-date=2008-11-20 |archive-date=March 6, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080306112131/http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111407aad.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Zeller notably exhibited that shooting touch at the 2018 [[Kentucky Derby Festival Basketball Classic|Kentucky Derby Festival Classic]], where he won the event's [[three-point field goal|three-point]] shooting contest.<ref name="UNC Bio"/>

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Zeller was listed as the No. 7 center and the No. 33 player in the nation in 2008.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Tyler-Zeller-53917;_ylt=AruiQaH3_Znmt75TRacxv_dGPZB4 Tyler Zeller Recruiting Profile]</ref>

==College career==
Zeller started the first two games of the [[2008–09 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|2008–09 season]] in place of the [[2007–08 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|previous season's]] consensus national Player of the Year, [[Tyler Hansbrough]], who was sidelined with a stress reaction in his right shin. In his first game, he scored 18 points in Carolina's season-opening win over [[Penn Quakers men's basketball|Penn]].<ref name="UK-UNC">{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=283230153 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081202065742/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=283230153 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 2, 2008 |title=Thompson powers Hansbrough-less UNC past Kentucky; Zeller hurts wrist |agency=[[Associated Press]] |publisher=ESPN|date=2008-11-18 |access-date=2008-11-20}}</ref>

The Tar Heels' next game, on November 18, was against another equally storied team, [[2008–09 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]]. The Heels scored a surprisingly easy 77–58 win over the Wildcats, but suffered another injury blow, this time involving Zeller. With 1:26 left in the game, Zeller went for a breakaway dunk off a turnover, but was fouled by Kentucky's Ramon Harris before he could score. Zeller fell to the floor awkwardly, got up, and was taken to the locker room holding his left wrist.<ref name="UK-UNC"/>

[[X-ray]]s showed that Zeller had broken both of the major bones in his lower left arm (the [[radius (bone)|radius]] and [[ulna]]). The day after the injury, he had surgery at [[UNC Health Care|UNC Hospitals]] to repair the broken bones.<ref name=Injury>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=3713121 |title=Broken wrist likely to sideline UNC forward Zeller for season |first=Andy |last=Katz |author-link=Andy Katz |publisher=ESPN|date=2008-11-19 |access-date=2008-11-20}}</ref>  In early January 2009, Zeller's cast was removed.

Zeller made his return during his freshman season on February 18, 2009, in the Tar Heels' home game against North Carolina State, playing 8 minutes and scoring 2 points.

As a sophomore, Zeller averaged 9.3 points per game on 52.1% shooting and 4.6 rebounds per game in limited action off the bench.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://carolinaupdate.com/north-carolina-basketball/roster_player/tyler-zeller |title=Tyler Zeller Career Stats |publisher=CarolinaDaily.com |access-date=January 6, 2011 |archive-date=March 8, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110308091256/http://carolinaupdate.com/north-carolina-basketball/roster_player/tyler-zeller |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Zeller averaged 15.7 points per game during his junior year. He shot 54.7% and averaged 7.2 rebounds per game. He had a more active role, playing an average of 28.1 minutes per game, significantly more than the 17.4 minutes per game during his sophomore campaign.<ref name="ESPN Profile">{{cite web|title=Tyler Zeller|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/6631/tyler-zeller|work=ESPN|access-date=27 March 2012}}</ref>

Zeller averaged 16.5 points per game on 55.3% shooting during his senior season. He also played an average of 28.2 minutes per game.<ref name="ESPN Profile"/>

Zeller was voted to the All-ACC First Team his senior year and was named the [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]].<ref>[http://www.tarheelblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030612aaa.html Zeller Named ACC Player Of The Year – NORTH CAROLINA OFFICIAL ATHLETIC SITE]. Tarheelblue.cstv.com (2012-03-06). Retrieved on 2012-03-12.</ref>  Zeller was also named a [[2012 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|second team all American]] by the [[Sporting News]] and the [[USBWA]] as a senior.  Both accolades made him eligible to have his jersey [[Honored North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball players|honored in the rafters]] of the [[Dean Smith Center|Smith Center]] at the conclusion of his college career.

==Professional career==

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2012–2014)===
Zeller announced that he was entering the [[2012 NBA draft]] along with North Carolina teammates [[Harrison Barnes]], [[Kendall Marshall]] and [[John Henson (basketball)|John Henson]]. He was selected by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] with the 17th pick in the draft, and was the fourth Tar Heel to be selected in the first round. He was subsequently traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on draft night, and signed his rookie scale contract with the Cavaliers on July 5, 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8133845/cleveland-cavaliers-sign-first-round-picks-dion-waiters-tyler-zeller|title=Cavaliers sign top draft picks Waiters, Zeller|date=July 6, 2012|website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

On October 11, 2013, Zeller underwent an emergency appendectomy procedure to remove his appendix and was subsequently ruled out indefinitely.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fearthesword.com/2013/10/12/4831272/tyler-zeller-emergency-appendectomy-out-indefinitely|title=Zeller Has Appendectomy, Out Indefinitely|first=Sam|last=Vecenie|date=October 12, 2013|website=Fear The Sword}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/cavaliers/2013/10/12/tyler-zeller-injury-appendicitis-appendectomy-cleveland-cavs/2972065/|title=Cleveland Cavaliers' Tyler Zeller has appendectomy|first=Adi|last=Joseph|website=USA TODAY}}</ref> He recovered from the surgery in time to face the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in the team's [[2013–14 Cleveland Cavaliers season|2013–14 season opener]] on October 30.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2013/10/do_you_remember_tyler_zeller_a.html|title=Do you remember Tyler Zeller? After missing the entire preseason, the Cavaliers center is working to return to form|first=The Plain Dealer|last=Jodie Valade|date=October 26, 2013|website=cleveland}}</ref>

On March 22, 2014, Zeller scored a then career-high 23 points in a 118–111 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400489906|title=Rockets 118–111 Cavaliers (Mar 22, 2014) Game Recap|website=ESPN}}</ref>

===Boston Celtics (2014–2017)===
On July 10, 2014, Zeller was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in a three-team trade that also involved the Cavaliers and the Brooklyn Nets.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-complete-three-team-trade|title=Celtics Complete Three-Team Trade|website=www.nba.com}}</ref> On December 5, 2014, he scored a then career-high 24 points on 10-of-11 shooting in a 113–96 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/games/20141205/LALBOS/gameinfo.html Zeller leads Celtics to 113–96 win over Lakers]</ref> He set a new career high on March 16, 2015, against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], scoring 26 points on 11-of-15 shooting to help the Celtics defeat the 76ers, 108–89.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/games/20150316/PHIBOS/gameinfo.html Celtics win 5th straight, 108–89 over 76ers]</ref>

Zeller started the 2015–16 season as the Celtics' starting center, but moved to the bench after just three games. Over the Celtics' first 25 games of the season, Zeller logged nine DNPs.<ref name=br>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/z/zellety01/gamelog/2016/|title=Tyler Zeller 2015–16 Game Log|website=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref> On December 16, he scored a season-high 12 points in a loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]], hitting 5-of-7 from the field in less than ten minutes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/celtics/post/_/id/4721378/stellar-tyler-zeller-not-enough-to-boost-tired-celtics|title=Stellar Tyler Zeller not enough to boost tired Celtics|date=December 17, 2015|website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Zeller began to see increased minutes in early February, recording two 16-point games on February 2 against the New York Knicks, and on February 5 against the Cleveland Cavaliers, both wins.<ref name="br" /> On February 7, he again set a season high, scoring 17 points in a 128–119 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/games/20160207/SACBOS/gameinfo.html Avery Bradley's 25 points helps Celtics beat Kings]</ref> On April 8, he tied a career high with 26 points in a 124–109 win over the Milwaukee Bucks.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/games/20160408/MILBOS/gameinfo.html Zeller scores 26, Celtics down Bucks 124–109]</ref>

On June 29, 2016, the Celtics tendered a qualifying offer to make Zeller a [[restricted free agent]].<ref name="Bulpett">{{cite news|url=http://www.bostonherald.com/sports/celtics/celtics_insider/2016/06/celtics_to_give_qualifying_offers_to_jared_sullinger_tyler|title=Celtics to give qualifying offers to Jared Sullinger, Tyler Zeller|last=Bulpett|first=Steve|date=June 29, 2016|work=[[Boston Herald]]|access-date=13 July 2016}}</ref> He went on to re-sign with the Celtics on July 27, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-five-players/|title=Celtics Sign Five Players|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 27, 2016|access-date=July 27, 2016}}</ref> On July 2, 2017, he was waived by the Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Keith P.|url=https://www.celticsblog.com/2017/7/2/15911968/boston-celtics-waive-tyler-zeller|title=Celtics waive Tyler Zeller|work=CelticsBlog.com|publisher=SB Nation|date=July 2, 2017|access-date=July 2, 2017}}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2017–2018)===
On September 12, 2017, Zeller signed a multi-year contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2017/09/12/brooklyn-nets-sign-tyler-zeller|title=NETS SIGN TYLER ZELLER|work=NBA.com|date=September 12, 2017|access-date=September 12, 2017}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2018)===
On February 5, 2018, Zeller was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in exchange for [[Rashad Vaughn]] and the rights to a future second-round draft pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-acquire-tyler-zeller-brooklyn-nets|title=BUCKS ACQUIRE TYLER ZELLER FROM BROOKLYN NETS|work=NBA.com|date=February 5, 2018|access-date=February 5, 2018}}</ref> On October 13, 2018, he was waived by the Bucks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com/wisconsin/story/milwaukee-bucks-request-waivers-on-center-tyler-zeller-101418|title=Bucks request waivers on center Tyler Zeller|work=FoxSports.com|date=October 13, 2018|access-date=October 14, 2018}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2019)===
On March 7, 2019, Zeller signed a 10-day contract with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-sign-tyler-zeller-10-day-contract|title=Hawks Sign Tyler Zeller To 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=March 8, 2019|access-date=March 8, 2019}}</ref> He was not retained by the Hawks upon the expiration of the 10-day contract.

===Memphis Grizzlies (2019)===
On April 5, 2019, Zeller signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-tyler-zeller-for-remainder-of-the-2018-19-season-190405|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Tyler Zeller for remainder of the 2018–19 season|work=NBA.com|date=April 5, 2019|access-date=April 6, 2019}}</ref>

=== San Antonio Spurs (2020) ===
On September 28, 2019, the [[Denver Nuggets]] had announced that Zeller had joined for training camp.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Labidou|first1=Alex|title=Denver Nuggets announce 2019 training camp roster|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-announce-2019-training-camp-roster-20190928|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 29, 2019|date=September 28, 2019}}</ref> On October 18, 2019, the Nuggets waived Zeller.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/tyler-zeller-let-go-by-denver/ | title=Tyler Zeller: Let go by Denver | date=18 October 2019 }}</ref>

On June 24, 2020, the [[San Antonio Spurs]] signed Zeller to their roster to complete the 2019–20 season following the restart of league play coming out of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-sign-tyler-zeller|title=Spurs sign Tyler Zeller for remainder of the 2019–20 season|work=NBA.com|date=June 24, 2020|access-date=June 24, 2020}}</ref> On December 2, Zeller was included in training camp roster with the Spurs,<ref>{{cite web |title=Spurs announce 2020–21 training camp roster |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-announce-2020-21-training-camp-roster |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 7, 2020 |date=December 2, 2020}}</ref> but was later waived by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] on December 19.<ref>{{cite web|title=Spurs waive Cam Reynolds and Tyler Zeller|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-waive-cam-reynolds-and-tyler-zeller|date=December 19, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 19, 2020}}</ref>

==Post-playing career==

After his NBA career, Zeller and his family moved to [[Pittsboro, North Carolina]], and he soon began serving as an assistant high school basketball coach at [[Northwood High School (North Carolina)|Northwood High School]]. He also participates in UNC alumni games.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.chathamnewsrecord.com/stories/tyler-zeller-entering-third-year-helping-northwood-basketball,16274|title=Tyler Zeller entering third year helping Northwood basketball|last=Rojas|first=Asheebo|newspaper=[[Chatham News & Record]]|date=2023-11-09|access-date=2023-12-20}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite news|url=https://chapelboro.com/sports/former-unc-star-tyler-zeller-coaching-at-northwood-high-mentoring-unc-signee|title=Former UNC Star Tyler Zeller Coaching at Northwood High, Mentoring Tar Heel Signee|last=Koh|first=Michael|date=2023-12-20|website=[[Chapelboro.com]]|access-date=2023-12-20}}</ref>

In 2024 Zeller joined the [[Tar Heel Sports Network]], serving as a color analysts for Tar Heels basketball games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Baxley |first=Rodd |title=Who is calling UNC basketball games on radio broadcasts with Jones Angell this season? |url=https://www.fayobserver.com/story/sports/college/acc/2024/10/15/unc-basketball-radio-tar-heel-sports-network-tyler-hansbrough-tyler-zeller-jones-angell/75691326007/ |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=The Fayetteville Observer |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Zeller is the son of Steve and Lorri Zeller, the nephew of former NBA player [[Al Eberhard]], and is the middle brother of former NBA players [[Luke Zeller|Luke]] and [[Cody Zeller|Cody]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Former UNC basketball standout Tyler Zeller learned stories from parents' book |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/unc/article25939081.html}}</ref>

Zeller is married and has 3 children.<ref name=":0" />
